subject: zoology_2
question_text: Give the dental formula of adult human beings.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.46, VSAQ 49. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Write the formula as a fraction, upper jaw over lower. A single row of digits is read as half an answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The formula
steps.why: The formula counts the teeth of one half of the upper jaw over one half of the lower jaw, so the full set is four times the digits shown.
common_mistakes: Writing 2123 alone. It must be written as a fraction, upper over lower.
Giving the milk teeth formula 2102/2102. That is the child's set.
steps.memory_tip: Two incisors, one canine, two premolars, three molars — 2123.
steps.margin_note: Write the fraction clearly. It is the whole first mark.
lines: The dental formula of adult human beings is

steps.label: What it denotes
steps.why: Reading the digits back as named teeth shows that the formula is a count and not a code.
common_mistakes: Saying it gives the total teeth. It gives one half of each jaw.
Naming premolars as molars. They are separate rows.
steps.memory_tip: Front to back: incisor, canine, premolar, molar.
steps.margin_note: Expand the four digits. Total 32 teeth is a good close.
lines: It denotes the arrangement of teeth in each

lines.text: An adult has 32 teeth in all
